analysis.title: NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA): Resetting the Chessboard: Moat Stays, Premium Repriced - Opportunity Ahead - Adj PT
key_insights: Mizuho reiterates Outperform on NVDA and cuts its price target to $220 from $250, about 35% upside from $162.85. It is a buyer ahead of the 11/17 (Tue) earnings report.

Jensen Huang stepping down as CEO preceded a stock decline of about 32% from the October peak (SOX down 23%) and a roughly $2T market-cap loss. Mizuho reads the extra 9 points of underperformance versus the SOX as the lost founder premium.

Mizuho sees a 6-7 month management overhang while NVDA comes under US government scrutiny. It points to Apple after Steve Jobs, where investor focus returned to execution and shares rose about 2,500% from 10/5/11 versus about 560% for the S&P 500.

Three-scenario FY29E analysis: loss of China revenue, share loss to AMD and AVGO, and lower ASP and gross margin. The base case cuts FY29E EPS about 17% from $21.83 to $18.04, which still implies 12% y/y EPS growth. Bull case EPS is $20.04 and bear case is $16.16.

At 12x P/E on the $18.04 base-case EPS (peer average about 23x), Mizuho derives the $220 target. The Exhibit 1 implied PTs are $281 (14x, bull), $220 (12x, base) and $162 (10x, bear). The bear-case PT is about equal to the current price, so Mizuho argues the stock is already near the bottom of its range.

China exposure in the scenario is deliberately aggressive. Interim CEO Colette Kress said the outlook assumed no China data center revenue. Mizuho models 1-3% of FY29E revenue lost, a $9B-27B revenue hit, from GPUs rerouted to Chinese AI labs via APAC/EU data centers or from tighter export controls.

Share loss scenario: Mizuho assumes 1-3% of AI accelerator spend shifts from a 68.6% NVDA baseline to AMD and AVGO, a $13-39B FY29E revenue hit. It argues NVDA's CoWoS and front-end capacity allocations and its balance sheet limit peers' gains.
Pricing scenario is the largest EPS risk: a 4-13% ASP decline (NVDA carries about a 20% price premium to AMD) compresses FY29E gross margin 400-1,200bps from 73% to 60-69%, cutting EPS 6-18%.

Succession: NVDA has a company-wide meeting planned for 11/18, after earnings. Mizuho lists internal candidates Colette Kress (CFO and interim CEO), Chris Malachowsky, Michael Kagan, Bill Dally and Ian Buck. Externally reported names are Tim Cook, Rene Haas and Johny Srouji.

Circular financing: Mizuho estimates NVDA holds about $100B of equity and warrants in the AI ecosystem, led by OpenAI (about $30B) and xAI (about $21B). It also has disclosed more than $160B of guarantees and commitments, mainly lease backstops and capacity purchases for neocloud data centers. Mizuho sees the risk as limited because chips are quality collateral and commitments are far below NVDA cash flow.

A CEO departure could hurt future neocloud financing deals, but Mizuho believes NVDA can keep using its balance sheet and FCF. It forecasts FCF of $384B in FY28E and $558B in FY29E, leaving capacity for buybacks.

Product roadmap: Vera Rubin and the Groq LPU are in production, with an ASP tailwind above 30% on VR200 NVL72 racks. Mizuho cites SemiAnalysis InferenceX results showing Vera Rubin NVL72 (FP4, GLM 5.2/5.3 744B agentic) ahead of AMD and TPU v7 on P90 interactivity.
Mizuho expects more than $1T of Blackwell plus Rubin revenue in C25-27E and a $3-4T TAM by 2030E. NVDA guides FY27E CPU revenue to about $20B, with FY28E potentially up more than 100% y/y.
Valuation: the $220 PT is about 14x FY28E EPS (prior about 16x) versus the SOX at about 15x. On C27E estimates NVDA trades at 10.6x P/E and 5.7x P/Sales versus peer averages of 23.1x and 7.2x.

Bull and bear cases outside the scenario work: bull PT $330 (about 17x upside FY28E EPS of $19.28) and bear PT $130 (about 19x downside FY28E EPS of $13.97). These assume a bigger macro AI cycle up or a macro AI breakdown.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $220 from $250 on a lower multiple (about 14x FY28E versus about 16x) after the CEO departure, while keeping Outperform. Mizuho says the stock already reflects the key-person loss and China, share and pricing scenarios.
Cited as a peer that could take NVDA share through faster onboarding at frontier clouds. Mizuho's peer table shows a $610 PT, with the stock at $524.02 on 11/13.
Named with AMD as a potential share gainer as ASIC performance narrows the gap. Mizuho's peer table shows a $530 PT, with the stock at $344.96 on 11/13.
Appears in the peer valuation table at 14.5x C27E P/E, price $130.37.

sector_views.rationale: Mizuho sees NVDA leading the AI race and valued attractively, with the sector selloff (SOX down 23% from the October peak) leaving valuation low relative to the roadmap.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports FQ3 FY27 (October quarter) on 11/17 (Tue). Mizuho estimates non-GAAP EPS of $2.48E versus Street consensus of $2.47E, and revenue of $109.93B (estimate) versus Street consensus of $109.09B. These are estimates, not reported figures.
Mizuho non-GAAP EPS estimates by fiscal year: FY27E $9.30 (Street $9.33), FY28E $16.07 (Street $15.90), FY29E $21.83 (Street $21.44). FY27 Q1 $1.87A and Q2 $2.22A are reported non-GAAP actuals.
Mizuho expects upside at the 11/17 print. The company-wide meeting on 11/18 may update the CEO search and technology roadmap.
FY28E revenue/EPS is estimated up about 71%/73% y/y with gross margin above 72%. The base scenario for FY29E implies revenue/EPS up about 17%/12% versus 34%/36% before the scenario impacts.
Mizuho's FY28E free cash flow forecast is $384B and its FY29E forecast is $558B, versus $225.9B estimated for FY27E.

trade_ideas.description: Buy NVDA ahead of 11/17 earnings, Outperform with $220 PT
trade_ideas.rationale: Mizuho sees the roughly 32% pullback and $2T market-cap loss as more than reflecting the key-person loss and its China, share and pricing scenarios, with a strong roadmap ahead.
trade_ideas.risk: Tighter China export restrictions, share shifts to AMD and AVGO ASICs, regulatory hearings, and failing to name a credible CEO.

risk_factors: Loss of restricted revenue from GPUs (GB200/300) rerouted to China or accessed by Chinese AI labs, and tighter restrictions if controls are lacking
NVDA leadership challenges at a crucial time, with potential share shifts as peers' ASICs narrow the gap or AMD onboards faster at frontier clouds
House and Senate hearings, more supervision and regulation
Failure to find a credible CEO, plus a 6-7 month management overhang
Pressure on neocloud financing, with circular financing and backstop worries tying NVDA to the financial condition of AI labs and neoclouds
Competitive pressure on ASP and gross margin, with NVDA carrying about a 20% price premium to AMD
Limited CoWoS capacity at TSMC, Taiwan geopolitical tension, potential FTC lawsuits, and a pullback in AI server spending
geopolitical: Possible escalation of US export restrictions on GPUs (GB200/GB300) rerouted to China or accessed by Chinese AI labs through APAC and EU data centers
House and Senate hearings, more supervision and regulation as NVDA comes under the US government microscope after the CEO departure
Taiwan tension and limited CoWoS capacity at TSMC listed among risks
Chinese shipments have yet to resume following re-approval of shipments by the US government

tension_points.bull_case: The roughly 32% decline from the October peak already reflects the lost founder premium. NVDA still leads merchant AI GPUs with a Blackwell/Rubin roadmap and about $384B FY28E FCF. Even the base scenario implies 12% FY29E EPS growth and a $220 PT, about 35% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: A 6-7 month management overhang under US government scrutiny, possible loss of rerouted China revenue ($9B-27B), 1-3% share loss to AMD and AVGO, and a 4-13% ASP decline that would cut gross margin to 60-69%. The bear scenario gives a $162 PT, about equal to the current price.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tighter export restrictions on rerouted GPUs, share shifts as ASICs narrow the gap, hearings bringing more regulation, or failure to name a credible CEO.

tension_points.bull_case: Chips serve as quality collateral, commitments are well below NVDA cash flow, and compute demand remains well above available supply.
tension_points.bear_case: NVDA holds about $100B of equity and warrants and more than $160B of guarantees and commitments, concentrated in neoclouds and AI labs. That ties NVDA's risk to the financial condition of the AI ecosystem.
